00150.name: Video format: width, height, rate denominator, rate numerator, ...
00150.evidence: Fields 0-3 in all ALL files: 3840,2160,1,25 (UHD 25p) / 1920,1080,1,25 (HD 25p) / 3840,2160,1001,30000 (UHD 29.97p) / 4096,2160,1001,30000 (4K DCI 29.97p) / 4096,2160,1001,60000 (4K DCI 59.94p); frame rate = numerator / denominator. Field 14 changes with the format (UHD 25p 5, HD 25p 8, UHD 29.97p 6, DCI 29.97p 4, DCI 59.94p 3) - probably the recording format/codec entry; fields 16 and 18 differ only in the HD file (7 and 1); the remaining fields are constant (1,1,0,8,0,0,0,1,1,1 ... 60) | Test files: 013.ALL = 012.ALL with 1080p/59.94 -> 1920,1080,1001,60000 and field 14 = 9; 014.ALL = 013.ALL switched XAVC-I -> XAVC-L -> 3840,2160,1001,60000 with fields 7 (8->4), 9 (0->11), 11 (1->5), 12 and 13 (1->0), 14 (9->13), 16 (0->1) changed, i.e. fields 7, 9, 11-13, 14 and 16 carry the codec/format entry | 014.ALL: the camera itself switched to 3840x2160 59.94p when the codec was changed to XAVC-L (confirmed by the user) | 015.ALL (014 switched to MPEG HD422, 1920x1080 60i): 1920,1080,1001,60000 (rate stays 59.94 = field rate) with field 4 = 0 (interlaced; 1 in all progressive files), field 7 = 8, field 9 = 3, fields 11/12/13 = 0,0,1, field 14 = 0, field 16 = 2. Codec pattern in field 16: 0 = XAVC-I (013), 1 = XAVC-L (014), 2 = MPEG HD422 (015); field 9: 0 / 11 / 3; field 11: 1 / 5 / 0; field 7: 8 / 4 / 8 | 016.ALL (RAW, 4096x2160 59.94p external) and 017.ALL (RAW & XAVC-I): 00150 describes only the internally recorded format (1920x1080 59.94p, XAVC-I fields 7/9/11-13, index 9); field 16 = 6 for RAW and 7 for RAW & XAVC-I (also in 002.ALL, whose field 18 = 1 is probably a RAW output variant). The RAW output format itself is not in 00150 (constant 4096x2160 59.94p in 016/017, the user's setting). | 018.ALL (RAW & XAVC-L) = codec index 8, internal 1920x1080 59.94p with XAVC-L fields 7=4, 9=11, 11=5, 12=1, 13=1, 14=0; 019.ALL (RAW & MPEG HD422) = codec index 9, internal 1280x720 59.94p with the MPEG fields 7=8, 9=3, 11=0, 12=0, 13=1, 14=0. Codec indices confirmed: 0 XAVC-I, 1 XAVC-L, 2 MPEG HD422, 6 RAW, 7 RAW & XAVC-I, 8 RAW & XAVC-L, 9 RAW & MPEG HD422 | 020.ALL (ProRes 422 HQ) = codec index 10, 021.ALL (ProRes 422) = codec index 11; both 1920x1080 29.97p with fields 7=8, 9=14, 10=4, 11=6, 12=1, 13=1 and format index 18 (HQ) / 19; additional changes when switching from RAW & MPEG HD422: 00173 field 1 (0 -> 1), 00283 (1 -> 0), 00407 (0 -> 1), 00426 (1 -> 0), 00454 (frame rate class 2 -> 1) | Files 022/023/024 (RAW only): field 17 = RAW output format index (0 = 4096x2160 59.94p, 1 = 4096x2160 29.97p, 3 = 2048x1080 59.94p; 2, 4, 5 inferred from the manual's list order 4096: 59.94/29.97/23.98, 2048: 59.94/29.97/23.98); field 22 = frame rate limit of the imager mode (60 Normal, 120 2K Center; copy of 00151 first field; not the S&Q default, see 00151); with RAW output 29.97p the internal rate follows (29.97p, format index 8) | 002.ALL (PAL-typisch 25p, field 17 = 0): the index is a list position, in the PAL list presumably 0 = 4096x2160 50p, so the NTSC labels are only valid for NTSC rates | Block 1 (025-027): with S&Q Motion switched on the camera forces field 17 to 3 (RAW output 2048x1080 59.94p) even for XAVC-I; field 22 is the default S&Q frame rate of the current format (60, or 120 with RAW 2K), 00151 first field is the chosen S&Q frame rate | 029.ALL (014 with Video Format 1920x1080 59.94P 50, XAVC-L; the 50 is the bit rate in Mbps, not 50 Hz; the camera was in NTSC mode, PAL needs a reboot): 1920,1080,1001,60000 with the XAVC-L fields 7=4, 9=11, 11=5 and 12/13 = 1 (UHD XAVC-L 014 has 0), index 14 = 0 (as in 018); side effects: ALL 00158 4 -> 2 (also seen when S&Q was switched on, 025), 00282 second field 0 -> 3

widget.note: Choose the codec first, then the format (resolution/frame rate); the list shows only the formats known for the codec. When the codec changes, a format with the same resolution and frame rate is chosen, otherwise the first one in the list. With RAW the RAW is stored externally only; the resolution here is the internally recorded format. Choosing a format also sets the values that move with it (e.g. Imager Scan Mode) from the sample files. Not every combination is possible on the camera; only formats known from files are offered. The RAW output is a position in the list of the camera menu (NTSC); with PAL (50p/25p) the same number means the PAL counterpart. Formats marked '– assumption' come from the menu lists of the manuals (NTSC and PAL; the 35/25 Mbps bit-rate variants are missing); only resolution, frame rate and scan are set, the format index (field 14) and the companion values (00175 etc.) are not checked.
